editorial:
Imagine arriving in a quiet town like San Ramon as a new nun, only to be thrown straight into a nightmare. You follow Ophelia, who finds herself fighting for the life of a pregnant woman possessed by a demon. The vibe is dark and tense from the start, making you feel the pressure she is under. Instead of just following the old rules of priest-led movies, this story puts a woman in charge of the battle against evil, which gives the whole plot a fresh and scary energy that keeps you leaning in.

You will love how the tension builds up and the surprising twists that happen when you think the danger is over. The acting is solid and the scares feel real, though some parts of the story move a bit slowly in the middle. If you enjoy spooky stories with a Latin American twist, you should definitely check this out. It looks great in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, but if you are a movie collector, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your shelf is the way to go for the best picture quality.
endingExplained: At the end, you find out that the demon did not actually leave. The evil spirit uses the unborn baby as a way to stay in the world. Even though Ophelia thinks she won the fight, the twist shows that the demon has successfully switched bodies. The movie wraps up with the scary realization that the evil presence is now inside the child, meaning the nightmare is just beginning for everyone involved.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves possession stories and creepy church settings.
